chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn Faďďāl, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Abī Nāb Ḥasan ibn ‘Aťiyyāh, who said:
I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about performing Ghusl when going to the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him). He replied, “Performing Ghusl is not obligatory.”

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ: It is not obligatory upon you

ai.seo_question: Is Ghusl required before visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) does not possess the status of a *majnun* (ritually impure) place requiring a full ritual bath (*ghusl*) for entry, thereby distinguishing it from specific contexts like entering the Prophet's mosque in Medina or major mosques where *ghusl* is recommended. This ruling underscores the spiritual purity of the Ahl al-Bayt's shrines, allowing visitors to maintain ease in devotion without the burden of obligatory purification rituals, while still encouraging *ghusl* as a highly recommended act of honor (*ta'zim*).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn Faďďāl, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir, from Abī Nāb Ḥasan ibn ‘Aťiyyāh, who said:
I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) about performing Ghusl when going to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.). Imam (a.s.) replied, “Performing Ghusl is not obligatory.”
